candidates.rationale: RemSpec is the existing public abstraction for implementation-specific remainder behavior and its panic-safety domain.
risks: rem_req must encode zero-divisor and signed overflow cases for concrete integer implementations.

candidates.rationale: RemAssign is independent of Rem and permits arbitrary mutation; vstd has no assignment-specific opt-in model relating old(self) and final(self).
risks: Equating final(self) with Rem::rem on old(self) would be unsound for custom implementations.

candidates.rationale: ShlSpec models implementation-specific shift behavior, while shl_req captures valid shift-count requirements.
risks: Each supported Self/Rhs combination needs a ShlSpecImpl, including its shift-count bound.

candidates.rationale: ShlAssign does not require consistency with Shl and supplies no universal relation for the mutation; no assignment-specific vstd abstraction exists.
risks: Relating final(self) to Shl::shl on old(self) would overconstrain valid custom implementations.
